messages:
Maya Chen: FYI - noticed a regression on host ingress p99 after yesterday's routing tweak, looks like ~15% on long streams.
Liam R: ugh, saw that in the dashboards too. any obvious hotspots from flamegraphs?
Maya Chen: attaching quick trace snippet, but preliminary profile points to repeated proto header parsing + small-message syscall overhead when streaming chunks under 512B.
Jorge P: can you paste the trace? also which path — http1 vs grpc?
Maya Chen: grpc only, specifically grpc unary/stream mix where we still call parse_header + validate for each framed chunk.
Maya Chen: ```
# simplified stack top
ingress.read_frame
proto.unpack_headers
tokenizer.tokenize_inline
kvcache.lookup_if_prefix
writev_flush
```
Sofia K: interesting — the tokenizer step shouldn't run for every tiny frame. Is our framer coalescing disabled on that path?
Liam R: iirc the framer coalescing flag got toggled in the canary: ENABLE_ASYNC_WINDOWING=false -> true in prod. maybe that changed write batching semantics.
Maya Chen: exactly, toggled it back locally and p99 dropped ~12%. but we still see overhead from header validation calls that are expensive on hot paths.
Jorge P: could be double-parse: we call proto.unpack in gateway and again in host-proxy. add a fast-path to mark already-validated frames?
Sofia K: +1. maybe sticky metadata on request object: if frame.origin==gateway and gateway-sig present, skip header re-parse.
Liam R: watch out for security audits — need to ensure signature chain validated. but we can have a cheap verif bit set by gateway when it's safe.
Maya Chen: also saw KV cache churn when small frames arrive interleaved across many requests. kvcache eviction noise adds syscalls.
Jorge P: hmm try sharding the small-frame buckets in kvcache so hot prefixes don't evict everything. also consider LRU windows per connection.
Sofia K: another low-cost win: avoid calling tokenizer.tokenize_inline for frames that match "prefetched-prefix" — use a single memcmp before tokenize.
Maya Chen: patched a local PoC with memcmp fast-path + gateway verif bit, re-ran perf: p99 down 18%, median unaffected. will push benchmark numbers later.
Liam R: sweet. can you share the PoC snippet? also open a short PR for the verif bit with an integration test.
Maya Chen: PoC snippet:
```go
// fast-path: if gatewaySigned && bytes.HasPrefix(frame, cachedPrefix) {
//   return cachedTok
// }
```
Maya Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
infra-bot: deploy-canary started for runtime/ingress-window-fix (build: 2026.3.7-ix)
Sofia K: let's keep an eye on grpc_stream_write latency on canary; also add a metric for header-parse calls/sec.
Jorge P: i'll prototype a kvcache small-bucket shard tomorrow. should reduce eviction stutter.
Liam R: can we add a short perf test that simulates many tiny frames across many connections? current benches focus on large-batch flows.
Maya Chen: yes, i'll add a test harness that drives 1k conns with 50-200B frames and measure p50/p95/p99 for parse+tokenize.
Sofia K: thanks all. if canary looks good we'll roll to stable and follow up with a deeper kernel-selection audit (seems orthogonal but worth checking). :thumbsup:
